1.explanation:
1. RadioButton.js – the RadioButton component itself must be updated to accept a new readOnly boolean prop in its signature and propTypes, apply a distinct CSS class when readOnly is true (e.g. `${prefix}--radio-button--readonly` on the wrapper or input), and prevent interactions (e.g. treat readOnly similarly to disabled but with separate styling).
2. RadioButton.stories.js – the Playground story must expose the readOnly prop in its argTypes so developers can toggle and preview the read-only state in Storybook, and a default story for readOnly should be added for copy-and-paste.

By focusing on the component and its stories, you satisfy the acceptance criteria: implement the prop, add styling, enable playground control, and prepare for RTL and unit tests. Tests will then be updated in __tests__ and e2e files to check the readOnly class and keyboard/navigation behavior, but the core fix lives in these two files.
1.bug_scenario: The user has added a new “readOnly” prop to the RadioButton component in their app and expects the component to render in a non-interactive, read-only style (per their design mockups). However, the existing RadioButton implementation does not handle a readOnly prop specially—it simply spreads any extra props onto the <input>, and since native radio inputs don’t support a readonly attribute, the button remains fully interactive and unstyled. To satisfy the acceptance criteria (new read-only prop, visual styling, storybook control, tests), several files will need updates.

2.explanation: 1. RadioButton component (RadioButton.js) needs to explicitly handle a readOnly prop: we must add it to propTypes, include a CSS class (e.g. `${prefix}--radio-button--readonly`) in wrapperClasses, prevent state changes in handleOnChange when readOnly is true, and forward the attribute to the <input>. 2. wrapperClasses variable is where styling classifications live, so it must include the read-only modifier. 3. The Playground story in RadioButton.stories.js must be updated to expose the readOnly control and include default/read-only examples. 4. The unit test file RadioButton-test.js must gain a new `it('should render as read-only', …)` test to verify the class name, attribute, and blocking of onChange when readOnly is set. 5. The e2e visual regression test (RadioButton-test.e2e.js) needs a new snapshotStory/test block for the read-only story to catch any styling regressions visually.
2.bug_scenario: The images and repro code show that when a consumer passes the readOnly prop into <RadioButton>, nothing changes visually or functionally—instead of rendering a non-interactive, “read-only” appearance (per the design spec’s color, spacing, and structure for a read-only radio), the component still behaves and looks like a normal, editable radio button. The spec images demonstrate the exact disabled‐look styling and vertical/horizontal spacing that should apply to read-only variants, but the implementation in RadioButton.js doesn’t handle readOnly, the stories don’t expose the new prop, and neither the unit tests nor the visual regression tests cover it.
